The numbers behind enterprise fintech’s
best quarter in over two years
Enterprise fintech may have turned the corner.
The sector delivered its strongest fundraising
quarter since Q1 2023, with $6.1 billion raised
and a 19% YoY increase. One key trend: Deal
volume fell 13% to 351 transactions, but median
deal sizes moved 29% higher to $6.5 million,
largely thanks to AI companies commanding
premiums. Meanwhile, IPO momentum is
building, with Circle's massive $6.4 billion debut
leading the charge, alongside consumer fintech
IPOs from eToro and Chime.
PitchBook data reveals that the CFO stack is
emerging as a winner from AI innovation,
capturing $1.8 billion across 90 deals, as
investors bet big on the opportunities to
automate manual finance and back-office tasks.
Yet, venture-growth deals also proved that
mature fintech infrastructure remains a priority
bet, as seen with Plaid’s $575 million raise,
Rippling’s $460 million Series G, and Airwallex’s
$301 million Series F. 
Get the complete picture with our Q2 2025
Enterprise Fintech VC Trends report, featuring
our comprehensive analysis and data
breakdowns. New this quarter: We are launching
an additional deal-sourcing resource in the
report that tracks stealth startups and executive
moves—the early signals that often precede the
start of a new venture.
